evals.prompt: Set up my outbound. We're Acme, we sell payroll software.
evals.expected_output: Should look for an existing outbound-context.md first. Should not invent the value proposition from one line. Should ask for material (website, deck, customers) or ask ONE question, not a numbered list. Should not write the file before the user confirms a draft.
assertions: Looks for an existing context file first
Does not invent customers, proof or numbers
Asks one question per turn, not a list
Does not write the file before confirmation

evals.prompt: Here's our site copy: 'We help 5-50 person logistics companies in Mexico cut fuel costs 12% with route optimization. Clients: TransMex, Rutas del Norte.' Our sales deck says we target enterprise fleets of 500+ trucks. Build my outbound context.
evals.expected_output: Should draft the value proposition and ICP from the copy. Should flag the contradiction between 5-50 person companies and 500+ truck enterprise fleets and ask the user to resolve it. Should not pick one silently.
assertions: Drafts sections from the given material
Flags the size contradiction between site and deck
Asks the user to resolve it instead of choosing
Uses the real customer names, invents none

evals.prompt: Write the voice section. Here are my messages: 'thanks!', 'ok sounds good', 'hey Ana, saw your post on hiring SDRs, we did the same last year, happy to share what worked'.
evals.expected_output: Should drop the one-liners. Should say that one real message is not enough evidence (needs about 10 across 5 conversations) and leave the voice section marked as not enough samples, or ask for more.
assertions: Says the sample is too small for a voice section
Does not write a voice profile from one message
